title: two_providers_over_jmap_only hangs: the runtime goes idle with the test still waiting
description:
Seen in the full-suite run of 2026-11-27 (12 test binaries at once). The test ran for 1 h 36 min with 3 seconds of CPU and no output after its first minute, and had to be killed for the run to finish. It is not slowness: run alone, immediately afterwards, it passed in 4.08 s.

THE WAIT IT IS IN. Its own line, lost to cargo's capture in the suite and seen in the standalone run: "waiting for fanout to reach 01M8FKN3M80RXKSQ42RMP53CD8". A fanout delivery to the other provider never arrives.

EVIDENCE, from the live process before it was killed (/proc/<pid>/task/*/comm and wchan): 22 threads, one reactor thread in ep_poll, every worker thread and both sqlx-sqlite workers parked in futex_do_wait, 5 sockets still open. An idle runtime with the test's future still parked is a lost wake-up, and load changes the interleaving that provokes it. A debugger could not be attached (ptrace_scope=1, no sudo), so the await is named by the test's own line and not by a backtrace.

NOT THE REFUSAL RATE LIMITING of bead mimid-sami, which is in the same working tree: all seven of its call sites keep their control flow outside the new conditional, so a suppressed line changes no behaviour, and this test waits on no log line.

RELATED. Bead mimid-67e0 is the same family: calls_across_two_providers kept failing on a guessed deadline, and commit 01ea50aa ("test: wait on events, not clocks") replaced those deadlines with event waits across the suite. A lost wake-up that a deadline used to turn into a flaky failure now turns into a hang, which is the intended trade -- the hang says the condition never held -- but it leaves the suite unable to report. Whether this is the same underlying bug as mimid-67e0.1 and mimid-67e0.2 is not known.

NEXT. Provoke it under load rather than giving it a deadline: the suite in parallel, or that binary against a loaded machine, with RUST_LOG=info into a file. The question is which side dropped the fanout: the hub's delivery task, the peer's acceptance, or the follower's notify.
notes:
FOUND, 2026-11-27, commit 97876997 in worktree agent-a6c1fc85753706224. Not production: the test's wake-up source died with the provider it restarted.

Jmap::open took provider.follower().appended_sender() once, at account creation (jmap_two_providers.rs:289). Step 4b stops b and boots it again, and Provider::boot builds a new Follower, so Follower::new makes a new broadcast channel. From step 4b on, bob_jmap held the sender of the dead follower's channel. Jmap::next subscribes to it and awaits only when a read found nothing, so the test passes whenever the read overtakes the fanout and parks for good when it does not. Holding the sender keeps the channel open, so the await cannot even end in Closed. The two waits that need the announcement after the restart are step 6's proposal fanout and step 9's external-Commit fanout: both reach b only by /notify from a, where bob's own requests are stored by store_accepted during the request itself.

PROVED THREE WAYS.
1. Deterministic unit regression, an_announcement_handle_outlives_a_restart: take the handle, restart b, subscribe, accept one /notify (which stores and announces before it returns), try_recv. Against the old behaviour try_recv returns Empty and the test FAILS; with the fix it passes. No clock.
2. The hang on demand: one line, b.script(&[Fault::Refuse]) before step 6's Room/update, makes a's first delivery of the proposals 503 so bob's read must come back empty. Pre-fix that run was killed at 120 s (EXIT=124) after six 'waiting for fanout' lines, with 0.14 s of CPU, the main thread in futex_do_wait, the reactor in ep_poll and the sqlx workers parked: the bead's signature. Post-fix the same run passes in 69.14 s on a machine at load 64.
3. Without the scripted fault the test passes pre-fix on this machine, which is why it is 2-of-3 in the suite and not 3-of-3.

RULED OUT by reading, each with its reason. The hub's fanout re-arms: on a transient failure deliver_due loops, re-reads outbox_heads, and returns the row's next_attempt_at, which the worker sleeps on; Notify::notify_one keeps a permit, so a wake while the worker is busy is not lost, and both enqueue sites (submit.rs:156, update.rs:324) wake after the row is committed. Follower::store_fanout announces every new seq inside the awaited call. The JMAP change bus is not on this path: the test waits on the follower's channel, not the bus. No dropped JoinHandle and no watch sender are involved.

FIX AND COST. Provider::appended hands out an Appended handle that resolves the running stack's channel when a receiver is taken, and boot replaces that channel. Cost: a receiver taken while the provider is stopped still hears nothing, so a reader has to take one per wait, which Jmap::next and Inbox::next already do. Follower::appended_sender now documents that the channel is the follower's own.

NOT KEPT: the Fault::Refuse line. It makes the integration test exercise the interleaving deterministically, but a reintroduced bug would hang it again rather than fail it, which is what left the suite unable to report. The unit test fails instead.
